reading_rules.text: Stage 4 starts from the observations, not the verses (researcher, #2526 Q7, 2026-11-21): the subgroups and the stage 3 observations on them are the input, the behaviours are discovered from analysing them, and the base data is read back into only occasionally. Every finding of step 3.1 or 3.2 rests on named observations (a traced node on each, with an occurrence node as well) and its occurrence nodes lie within the occurrences those observations cover; an occurrence outside them is allowed only where the finding records a read-back (the verse and why). Each node has a role from reading.node_roles other than lexical, chosen by the reading. A 3.3 finding carries nodes on the occurrences of both sides in the shared verses.

A finding of a stage 4 row is checked by the rules of observationrecord.check and check_item_parts (kind, text, basis, route, parts.item and what the item needs, node roles, collection of each node) and by RG, RW and RS, which are not restated here: one observation for each finding, never a duplicate, with a node on each word it applies to (RO11, RW-03); founded in the observations and never a restatement of the verse (B:131); parts.item is one of the items the row's item uses (cfg_setting layer.reading). An observation whose nodes all bear on an act is refused: those words are nodes of the observation of the act. A finding is a building block of a behaviour and never a claim (stage 5).

Nothing the step reads is lost on the way to stage 5. Step 3.1: every stage 3 observation of the subgroup is rested on by a finding or declared in not_used with its reason in words. Step 3.2: every 3.1 observation of the collection is gathered into a behaviour (a traced node on it from a flag finding of type discovery) or declared in not_gathered with its reason, and the row has at least one behaviour unless it is recorded as none with its reason. A behaviour names and gathers; it makes no claim about what the behaviour is.

An earlier inner-being observation with a node on the occurrences of a 3.1 row (any stage but lexical, layer-1, layer-2 and layer-3) is shown in the pull for information and may be actioned in `existing`: accepted, modified, deleted, merged or left, each with its reason, through observationrecord (RW-01, RW-09); nothing is demanded of it, and it counts for nothing in the check. A row answered again withdraws its earlier observations with the reason. Every older live observation with a node on an occurrence of the row is answered in fill.older at the record of the row (RW-13); this rule's `existing` actions of stage 4 are unchanged.
One observation per finding, never a duplicate description; a finding applying to several verses or words carries several nodes, each with the word's role in it.

Read outward from the verse, not inward from the scope's question. First record everything the verse carries, each with where it bears (chapter, thread, signpost); answer the scope's question last. A verse often has two or three significances, and none is dropped.
Read the verse in its passage and genre; name the speaker; explore figures for what they say about the inner being; take paired and opposite acts together. Restating a verse is not reading it.

Find the main inner-being operation, and give every word that bears on it its role in this finding (cfg_setting reading.node_roles): characteristic, qualifier and what it gives the characteristic, object or content, relational target, or enactment. A word read in the verse that holds nothing for the inner being is standalone. The role comes from this verse, never from the cluster tag. Where a standalone word proves to qualify a characteristic, it is a qualifier of it.

A qualifier gets no separate account of itself, but what it gives the characteristic it binds to is evaluated for its value and recorded as a qualification finding, applied by its nodes to the qualifier (role qualifier) and the characteristic (role characteristic). What it gives can vary widely: grade, nature, impact, size, relation, a measure, strengthening, ground, cause, object, setting or bait are examples, not a list (#2273 D9). A qualifier whose usage varies across contexts may earn its own reading later.
Record how the M-code words work together (a relational observation). Record any pointer outside the verse separately, without resolving it inline.

Record the parties: who bears the act, who causes it, who is acted on (source, target, impact, purpose), and the route (cfg_enum observation_route). A non-human being is never itself a HIB; a collective stays one HIB; an implied party is named as referential, never asserted.
Read the T3 operations, movement and force, negators (a refusal is an act), connectives, body parts, places, objects and nature for what they carry here; read every row, untagged ones too.

For every word that names an inner or bodily act, look at the original: the root's range in all three meaning sources read together, never one picked and the others dropped; the ESV renderings across its verses; whether the English adds or hides; the literal sense beside the rendering. Where more than one reading is open, record each, and mark the choice 'I read'.

Record each relevant word's face as it appears HERE: the circumstance in this verse and where the sense departs from the general gloss. Identifying and clarifying the face is lexical work; what the faces do for the inner being, and a double meaning in different scenarios, are layer 2 of the collection reading (layer-aspects-are-ledgered-and-never-left-open).
Never close a verse or item on 'not X'. A role label is never a verdict; the close records what the verse is. Silence about the inner being is a finding, recorded as data with its reason.
A phenomenon hidden behind a stated or refrained act may be named, with the verb, clause or stated silence that grounds it, and whether it is stated or read.
A literary or structural pattern is not an inner-being observation: log it as an open question instead. A human/divine comparison is recorded only where the text's own wording anchors it.
Keep the source of an interior state apart from the source of an enablement to act.
Morph is read, not carried: where occurrences of a word show different stems or voices, record whether the subject does, undergoes or causes the act.
A difference, or a specific inference, is its own observation, never folded into another.

A word that is only a homonym or a name, with no meaningful context, is recorded as such (tag no-human-context) and left. Data errors found while reading are flagged (tag data-error), not fixed in the reading.
The question catalogue's questions are prompts for the areas to explore. A question that does not apply is not answered, and no answer is manufactured beyond what the verse shows.
Faculty (heart, soul, spirit, mind) is reflected on at the end, over the scope, not per word.
Before reading the whole scope, read a few verses and have them checked.
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.

A reading records findings of eight kinds (cfg_setting reading.observation_parts; the kind is the tag): face, qualification, party, statement, link, use, term, silence. A finding holds its text, meaning, implication, basis, its structured parts (ib_observation.parts: item, and mode, polarity, flag_type or grounds where its item needs them; reading.observation_items) and, on a party or link finding, its route; its nodes hold the verse, the word, the occurrence, the collection and its subgroup, the word's role in the finding and the reading that applied it. The silence kind is not used by Analysis_phase_1: a surface with no inner-being role is not recorded.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
An observation about a word can be answered only by consulting this occurrence's verse, span and morph.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.

A flag raised in reading (needs adjacent context, a pointer) states its reason and what the follow-up must establish, and is carried to an open item, not resolved inline. Can't-resolve is recorded, never guessed (tag could-not-resolve).
Where the evidence points to more than one reading, each is its own observation with its own evidence.
A re-read includes the observations already recorded for the verse, so the reading sees prior findings and builds on them.
Where a verse ends up for a finding is recorded on the node (ib_node.disposition, cfg_enum observation_disposition: told, claim, held, data, context, withdrawn), with its reason or carrier.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

After recording, every observation is read back against the verse for sense. An uncertain one is recorded as uncertain (tag could-not-resolve, or basis read: 'I read'), never asserted. A rule found to be systematically wrong is raised as a config change with the learning, never worked round in the reading.

A word is read per its lettered Strong's code (its grain), never the bare lemma (B:113). The occurrences of a word with several senses are related per grain and never aggregated across grains: related verses are same-grain occurrences.

Content words carry the inner-being impact and are read even when no cluster tags them. Function words (particles, prepositions, conjunctions, suffixes, pronouns) get no observation of their own, except negators and connectives, which are read for what they do (RG-07). A T2 word never stands alone: it is read as the qualifier of what it binds to.

The words in cfg_setting reading.non_characteristic_strongs are never a verse's characteristic: superscription metadata and named external adversaries. They are read as standalone or as qualifiers. The list is per word, not per cluster, because a cluster can hold both kinds.

A tagged word that works adverbially in an occurrence (a noun with a preposition qualifying the predicate, as 'in the counsel of the wicked') is a qualifier there, not the verse's characteristic. The role is per occurrence: the same word may be the characteristic elsewhere.
In a simile, the predicates of the vehicle (the tree that yields, does not wither) are read for what they say of the one compared (the tenor), not as the vehicle's own acts.

An existing observation counts for a surface when its node names that occurrence (verse_lexical_id), or, with none, when the node's verse, Strong and surface match one occurrence only. A node that names a verse and no surface, or matches more than one occurrence, is set aside: it does not count for any surface.

When a verse is worked, every existing observation and node on it, of any stage, is checked against the verse by its wording. The stage is not an indication of the nature of an observation and is never used to filter. Each observation is accepted, modified (changed in place; the old value, the new value and the reason are kept in ib_observation_change), soft deleted (the `deleted` column, with the reason), merged (a duplicate description, into the observation that is kept) or, when its wording shows it is not verse understanding, left exactly as it is with the reason. The check's fixes are part of it and need no separate approval. Nothing is physically deleted.

A surface with no inner-being role in a verse has no observation of its own. A word read in the verse that holds nothing for the inner being has the role standalone, which is a role and not an absence; where it could be a qualifier it is read as the qualifier of the characteristic it serves.

The observations of a verse state what the verse shows, and Record enforces it from cfg_setting reading.observation_rules and reading.observation_items: an observation of a relevant surface carries parts.item (one of the nine items), is written as one of the kinds that item allows, on a basis the item allows (a read observation names its grounds), and carries what its item needs (polarity, mode, flag type; a party carries its route). The words that bear on an act are nodes of the observation of the act, never an observation of their own (bears_on_only_refused). Every surface with the role characteristic has each applicable item observed or stated absent with the reason; the verse always has an operation observation. A verse whose observations do not comply is not recorded (#2329).

For every surface with the role characteristic, the nine items of spec 4.2 (reading.observation_items) are each explored, and each applicable item is its own observation (parts.item), written once and applied to every characteristic it is true of by its nodes; a qualifier or shared observation carries nodes on every characteristic it covers. An item the verse does not show gets no observation and is stated absent on the surface (items_absent) with the reason; the meaning item is never absent. The operation item carries a mode (done, foreseen, commanded, negated, reported) and an action description of who or what does what, read from before and after as the verse itself states them (passage-level before and after are the claims process's); the verse always has an operation observation. A read observation (basis read) names its grounds in the words of the verse (parts.grounds). No observation restates the verse text (no run of more than reading.observation_items max_verse_words_copied words). The same text for all items is not an exploration of them. Which word is the characteristic is the verse's decision, never the cluster's (RG-03). The nuance pointers (reading.nuance_pointers) say where each nuance is recorded (#2329).

An observation is created with its marker (ib_observation.nature, from the item answered, cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature; a finding file never sets it) and every word node with the columns of layer.reading node_required. A column the data cannot give (layer.reading node_gap_columns: an empty morph in the source row, a surface with no placement in the collection index) is left empty and its reason is kept on the node (disposition_note); any other missing column refuses the whole file and nothing is written. A trace to a deleted observation is refused (IB-07).

Every older live observation with a live node on an occurrence of the row (a stage that is not the build's own) is answered in fill.older when the row is recorded, once: keep or restate (each with its marker), merge into a named observation, consume (live observations carry its meaning, stated in words, verified before it is deleted), delete as neither (comment first), or defer to a named collection (marked now; only the finding is left to that collection). An observation already marked by the validation, answered in a build or deferred is not asked again. A new observation whose text equals that of another live observation of the collection is refused, the other named. LayerCheck re-derives both from the tables. The end state of a collection's build is that every observation of its scope is marked and fixed or deleted, every word node complete or with its reason, and each deferral owned by a named collection.

A lookup of related data in the build or the validation is by an indexed column and takes a chunk of ids (cfg_setting layer.scan chunk); none runs once for each item of a list, and a statement that uses more work than layer.scan max_vm_ops is stopped and named, nothing written (lib/scanguard.py). The tests refuse a statement of the build whose query plan scans a table (layer.scan scan_ok lists the temporary tables a statement may scan).

rows.asks: What do the stage 3 observations of this subgroup (its definition, its Strong's enrichment, its pairings, qualifiers, entities, direction, relations and double meanings, with the stage 1 senses) show of the elements of a behaviour of the inner being: what is done and its mode, whether a refusal or a pursuit, what it is directed at, the outward act, the other party with the route, the circumstance, the chain of operations, and the dimensions of the working (what a qualifier or a variation of the word gives it, from the lexical variation the stage 3 observations record)? Each finding is one observation that rests on named observations (a traced node on each) and carries nodes on the occurrences those observations cover, with the role each has; an occurrence outside them is allowed only with a read-back (the verse and why). Every stage 3 observation of the subgroup is rested on by a finding or declared not used, with the reason. A finding is a building block and never a claim about the behaviour as a whole (stage 5).

interventions: Work from the observations: the stage 3 observations of the subgroup are the input, and the verses are base data read back only where an observation does not settle the point; a read-back is recorded (the verse and why).
Read the lexical variation (the different Strong's codes of a surface, the forms of a word, the double meanings) as the dimensions of how the working happens, not as a difference to be smoothed away.
A behaviour is discovered from the elements, not assumed from the subgroup: a subgroup may form one behaviour, part of one, join others, or form none.

Record building blocks only. A statement of what a behaviour is, is a claim and belongs to stage 5; stage 5 receives the observations and not the subgroups, so everything it will need from them is recorded here.
Check the original where an observation depends on the word's range (RG-08); do not force a meaning and never close on 'not X' (RG-10).

A word whose role is not its collection's is reclassified by the collection change procedure and the step reopens (B:129, B:134); a discovery outside the observations is recorded as a flag finding of type discovery and is not resolved inline (RW-07).

to_take_up.text: The surfaces of this group, mind on, minds on and setting your mind, share one kind of meaning in the dictionary: the mind's set or direction, a frame of thought directed to something. G5427 gives purpose, frame of thought, will and aspirations, and G5426 gives to think, to set one's mind on, to have a certain attitude. The three surfaces are the noun and the verb of one root and stand in two vers

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out. G5427 (purpose, frame of thought, will, aspirations; 2 occurrences, both in Rom 8:6) and G5426 (to think, to set one's mind on, to have an attitude; 2 occurrences, in Rom 8:5 and Mar 8:33) are the noun and the verb of one root, and each names the mind's set or direction. The codes that link the group to its usage are both, since the verses use them for th

The one qualifier that reaches a member of this group is the negator in Mar 8:33, which reaches the verb of the setting of the mind: Peter is said not to be setting his mind on what belongs to God, so the negation is of that directing and the verse then names the other direction, to what belongs to men. In Rom 8:5-6 the nouns and the verb are not negated or qualified by a word of the grammar; the

The entities named in the verses of this group are divine and human. In Mar 8:33 the disciples are named as those Jesus turns to, Peter is addressed, God and man are the two whose concerns the mind is set on, and Satan is addressed in the rebuke; in Rom 8:5-6 the flesh and the Spirit are named, and the persons are those who live by either. The verse of Mark names the persons, and the verses of Rom

The direction of the mind's setting is stated in two ways. In Rom 8:5-6 the mind is set by persons on the flesh or on the Spirit, and the verses state the outcome of each, death or life and peace, as following from the setting. In Mar 8:33 Jesus speaks to Peter, in the second person, of the direction of his mind, from God's concerns to men's. In every verse the one whose mind is set is the human s

may_rest_on_besides.text: In Rom 8:6 the noun names the mind's set or bent, the frame of thought that is directed to the flesh or to the Spirit; the verse makes it the thing that leads to death or to life and peace, and it stands twice, once for each direction.

In Rom 8:5 the verb stands for directing the mind to something: the people of the flesh direct it to the flesh's concerns and the people of the Spirit to the Spirit's; it is a directing of thought and not a conclusion reached.

In Mar 8:33 the verb is Jesus' charge to Peter, who directs his mind to what belongs to men and not to what belongs to God; it names where the mind is directed, and the verse sets the two objects against each other.

verses_of_the_subgroup.Mark.8.33: But turning and seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said, “ Get behind me, Satan! For you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of man.”
verses_of_the_subgroup.Rom.8.5: For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
verses_of_the_subgroup.Rom.8.6: For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.

to think, to mind; to be of opinion, Acts 28:22; Phil. 1:7; to take thought, be considerate, Phil. 4:10; to entertain sentiments or inclinations of a specific kind, to be minded, Rom. 12:16; 15:5; 1Cor. 13:11; 2Cor. 13:11; Gal. 5:10; Phil. 2:2; 3:16; 4:2; to be in a certain frame of mind, Rom. 12:3; Phil. 2:5; to imagine, entertain conceit, 1Cor. 4:6; to heed, pay regard to, Rom. 14:6; to incline to, be set upon, mind, Mt. 16:23; Mk. 8:33; Rom. 8:5; Phil. 3:15, 19; Col. 3:2

findings.text: In Rom 8:5 the mind is directed: those who live by the flesh and those who live by the Spirit each set their minds on the things of their own way. The act is a setting of the mind toward an object, stated as done by persons of either way of living, with the same verb for both.

In Rom 8:6 the setting of the mind is stated as the mind-set itself (the noun G5427, twice): a mind-set of the flesh and a mind-set of the Spirit. The verse gives the operation once for each side of the contrast and states what each issues in.

In Mar 8:33 the setting of the mind is negated for Peter: the negator stands 1 word before the verb and reaches it, so the act toward the things of God is stated as not being done, with the things of man as what the mind is on instead.
In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the setting of the mind is a pursuit of its object: the mind is directed toward the flesh or toward the Spirit, and the verses set the two against each other as alternatives.
In Mar 8:33 the act is a refusal as the verse states it: the setting of the mind on the things of God is negated and its opposite object is named in the same sentence.

The object of the setting is named in each verse as one of a pair of opposites: the things of the flesh against the things of the Spirit (Rom 8:5), the flesh against the Spirit (Rom 8:6), the things of God against the things of man (Mar 8:33). The direction does not change in kind across the three verses; only the pair differs.

In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the setting of the mind stands beside a way of living and its issue: living by the flesh or the Spirit goes with the mind-set, and the verse states death for the one and life and peace for the other. The stored data names no person in these two verses; the contrast is carried by the nouns flesh and Spirit.

Mar 8:33 is a rebuke: Jesus turns, sees his disciples, and says it to Peter. The setting of the mind is therefore named in a speech of correction aimed at one person in the hearing of the others, and the entities the stored data names in the verse are the disciples, God and man.
